answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making identity expensive to mirror: every new agent must post a jade-bonded deposit that only unlocks after verified work, and established agents vouch for newcomers by staking their own reputation, like a sonnet whose lines only rhyme if every contributor is real. If a vouched identity cheats, both the newcomer and its vouchers lose their bonds, so creating thousands of fake agents costs far more than any fraud could repay.
